# REST API

The REST API that @protobase/server generates, with its routes, access, filters, writes, batches and errors.

`@protobase/server` turns resource definitions into a Hono app that follows Google's API design conventions ([AIP-131 to 136](https://google.aip.dev/131), [158](https://google.aip.dev/158), [160](https://google.aip.dev/160)). It uses Web APIs only and runs on Node and Workers; the Node adapter lives in the example.

```ts
import { configExports, createAdmin } from '@protobase/server'
import { auth, authenticate } from './auth/auth' // Better Auth, see /reference/auth/
import * as config from './config'

const { resources, views } = configExports(config) // splits a config's index.ts exports
const admin = createAdmin({
  resources,
  views,                                            // optional, served by /meta
  db,                                               // Kysely<any> on Postgres
  authenticate,                                     // required: no development mode; anonymous only with that role
  auth,                                             // optional: mounts login at /api/auth/*
  functions,                                        // optional: your own endpoints at /api/functions/<name>, see /guides/api-functions/
  options: { statementTimeoutMs: 15_000, scanGuard: { mode: 'reject' } },
})
```

Run the ERP example with `bun run --cwd examples/erp serve` (port 8787, Better Auth login, organization 1 as tenant; `REQUEST_LOG=true` logs requests). Interactive reference: `/api/docs`; like `/api/openapi.json` it needs a bearer token, because the document lists what the caller may see and do. Every route answers `401` without a valid token; get one with `protobase token you@example.com`. A project whose roles define [`anonymous`](access.md#anonymous-access) serves the resources API to requests without a token as that role.

## Routes

`/api/v1/*` is resources only, so a table may be called `meta` or `docs`. The system endpoints (`/api/meta`, `/api/openapi.json`, `/api/docs`), the app's own [API functions](../guides/api-functions.md) (`/api/functions/<name>`), [file downloads](files.md#downloads) (`/api/files/<provider>/<path>`), [public forms](forms.md#routes) (`/api/forms/<name>`) and login (`/api/auth/*`) live beside it; the parent of `options.basePath` is where the system endpoints go.

Under `/api/v1`:

| Route | |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /{resource}` | list: `filter`, `order_by`, `page_size` (50, max 500), `page_token`, `fields`, `labels`, `photos`, `photos_order_by`, `count=exact` |
| `POST /{resource}:search` | same parameters as a JSON body (`fields` and `labels` arrays), for long filters |
| `GET /{resource}/{key}` | one record, with `ETag`; composite keys are `part,part`, each part percent-encoded |
| `POST /{resource}` | create, `201` with `Location` and `ETag` |
| `PATCH /{resource}/{key}` | partial update, `If-Match` required |
| `DELETE /{resource}/{key}` | soft delete when the resource has one ([AIP-135](https://google.aip.dev/135)); `If-Match` optional |
| `POST /{resource}:upload?field=&name=` | one file for a [file field](files.md#uploading), as the raw body or one multipart file part; `201 { value, file, derived, corrected? }`, where `value` is the ticket a write sends as the field's value; `413` over the field's `maxSize`, `415` for a type it does not take |
| `POST /{resource}/{key}:reveal` | `{ "field": "iban" }` gives `{ field, value }` of one [sensitive field](#sensitive-fields-and-audit), with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and publishes an audit event |
| `GET /{resource}/{key}:history` | the record's changes, newest first, for a resource with [history](history.md): `page_size` (20, max 100), `page_token`; see [Record history](#record-history) |
| `GET`, `POST /{resource}/{key}:comments`, `GET /{resource}/{key}:mentionable?q=` | the record's comments, newest first, adding one, and whom it may mention, for a resource with [comments](comments.md); see [Record comments](#record-comments) |
| `POST /{resource}/{key}:generate` | `{ "action": "<name>" }` runs an [AI action](ai.md#ai-actions) of the caller's view: the model writes its field, with the ETag the record was read with, and it answers the record as an update does |
| `POST /{resource}/{key}:undelete` | restores a soft-deleted record ([AIP-164](https://google.aip.dev/164)); `If-Match` optional; `409` when not deleted, `400` on hard-delete resources |
| `POST /api/v1:batchWrite` | many writes in one transaction, see [Batch writes](#batch-writes) |
| `GET /{resource}:facets?field=&filter=&limit=&label=` | `{ field, facets: [{ value, count }] }`, the `limit` most frequent values (100 by default, at most 1,000), never all of them; with `label`, a relation's facets carry the related record's name as `label`, as in [Related names](#related-names) |
| `GET /{resource}:aggregate?group_by=&sum=&average=&maximum=&filter=` | `{ group_by, groups: [{ value, count, sum }] }`: the records the whole filter finds, per value of `group_by`, each with its count and, with `sum`, `average` or `maximum` (one of them), that of a numeric field, `null` when no record of the group has one. Values come largest first, the first `limit` (100 by default, at most 1,000), with `label` as in `:facets`. A date or timestamp `group_by` is bucketed like `:series` instead (`granularity` `minute`, `5_minutes`, `15_minutes` or `hour` to `year`, `range` or `from` and `to`, `time_zone`), empty buckets included, and each `value` is the bucket's start; the response adds `granularity` and `time_zone`. With `split_by` (a filterable field of values), a date `group_by` also splits each bucket: the response adds `split_by` and `splits` (the `split_limit` largest values over the range, 8 by default and at most 100, ranked by the sum, else by count; `split_label` names a relation's values), and each group lists its `splits` with their count and sum, average or maximum. Unlike `:facets`, the filter's terms on `group_by` apply too, so the groups add up to what the filter finds |
| `GET /{resource}:series?field=&range=&granularity=&time_zone=&filter=` | `range` is `1h`, `24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `90d`, `1y`, `all`, or `from` and `to` (ISO); `granularity` `minute`, `5_minutes`, `15_minutes`, `hour`, `day` (the default), `week` or `month`. Buckets of minutes start on the clock's multiples of them |
| `GET /{resource}:histogram?field=&buckets=&filter=` | equal-width buckets of a numeric field |
| `GET /{resource}:map?latitude=&longitude=&zoom=&filter=&order_by=&fields=&labels=&photos=&photos_order_by=` | the records in a map's view, the bounding box being in `filter` (`lat >= 51.9 AND lat <= 52.1 AND lng >= 4.2 AND lng <= 4.5`), as `{ items, buckets, total_size }`; see [Maps](#maps) |
| `GET /{resource}:seek?position=&order_by=&filter=&page_size=&fields=&labels=&photos=&photos_order_by=` | the page at a row position (scrollbar jumps), with `next_page_token` and `prev_page_token`; same items as a list |
| `GET /api/meta` | resource, view and page models (fields carry `default`: `{ value }` or `{ db: true }`) and the caller's `permissions`; the `ETag` hashes both, so it differs per user; `If-None-Match` gives `304` |
| `GET /api/live?after=` | a `text/event-stream` of which records of the [live](live.md) resources the caller may read change, keys only; see [The stream](live.md#the-stream) |
| `POST /api/files:cleanup` | runs the [scheduled file deletes](files.md#deleting-files) that are due, for an admin; `{ deleted, kept }` |
| `GET /api/openapi.json`, `GET /api/docs` | OpenAPI 3.1 for the caller (only the resources, fields and operations their roles allow), and the Scalar reference |

Every response carries `X-Meta-Version`, the hash of the models, the Protobase version and the caller's roles; a client that sees it change (a model edit, an upgrade, a role change) refetches `/meta`.

`show_deleted=true` on list, `:search` (body) and get also returns soft-deleted records (soft-delete resources only, `400` otherwise).

A list returns `{ items, next_page_token, total_size_estimate }`, the estimate being the planner's, which reads no rows. `count=exact` adds `total_size`, counted through the indexes but no further than 10,000 matches: above that `total_size` is left out and the estimate stands. `next_page_token` is `""` on the last page, and a token only continues the `filter` and `order_by` it came from: with others the request fails with `400 invalid-cursor`. Items use field names, dates as ISO 8601 text, 64-bit integers and decimals as strings.

### Record history

`GET /{resource}/{key}:history` answers `{ items, next_page_token }` for a resource with `.history()`, and `404` for one without. It needs what a get needs, a soft-deleted record included. Each item is `{ id, at, operation, changed, before?, after?, actor, database_role }`: `before` and `after` hold only the fields the caller may read, never a sensitive or file field, `changed` names the changed fields the caller may read, and an update of only other fields is left out. `actor` is `{ id, name? }` for a write through the API, the name when the project's Better Auth knows the user, and `null` otherwise; `database_role` is the role that wrote. See [Record history](history.md).

### Record comments

For a resource with `.comments()`, and `404` for one without; each needs what a get needs. `GET /{resource}/{key}:comments` answers `{ items, next_page_token }`, newest first, a soft-deleted record included, with `page_size` (20, max 100) and `page_token`. Each item is `{ id, created_at, body, author, mentions }`, where `author` and each of `mentions` is `{ id, name? }`, the name when the project's Better Auth knows the user. `POST` with `{ "body": "...", "mentions": ["<user id>"] }` adds the caller's comment to a record that is not deleted and answers `201` with it: `body` is trimmed, `mentions` names at most 20 users, the caller dropped, and each is emailed. `GET /{resource}/{key}:mentionable?q=` answers `{ items: [{ id, name }] }`: at most 8 users whose name contains `q`, by name, who may read the record, without the caller. Its problems: `403 comment-needs-user` to a caller who is not signed in, on the `POST` and on `:mentionable`; `400 invalid-comment` for an empty body or one over 10,000 characters; `400 invalid-mention` for a mention of someone who may not read the record, which keeps nothing. See [Record comments](comments.md).

### Related names

A list holds a relation as the key of the record it points at. `labels` names those records in the same answer: `labels=place_id.name,agency_id.name` on a list, `:search`, `:seek` or `:map` adds `labels: { "place_id": { "12": "Amsterdam" }, "agency_id": { ... } }`, the `name` of each place and agency the page's items point at, by key as text. Each entry is a relation among the returned fields, to a resource with a single-field key, and the field of that resource that names its records, neither a file nor JSON; anything else is a `400`. The related records are read as the caller lists that resource, in one query per relation: its tenant, row filter, soft delete and readable fields apply. A record they cannot list, or whose field they cannot read, is not in `labels`, and neither is an empty name, so it goes by its key; a field they cannot read or that does not exist answers the same, so `labels` never tells it exists.

### Card photos

A list can bring each record's first photos in the same answer, as a cards display's [`photos`](ui-config.md#card-photos) shows them: `photos=listing_photos.listing_id.photo&photos_order_by=position` on a list, `:search`, `:seek` or `:map` adds `photos: { "12": [{ "uri": "public:…", "url": "…", "placeholder": "…" }, …] }`, the `photo` files of the first ten records of `listing_photos` whose relation `listing_id` points at each item, by its key as text, in `photos_order_by` order (their primary key breaking ties). An item without photos is not in `photos`. The entry names a resource, its relation to the listed one and its file field; a malformed entry, or `photos_order_by` without it, is a `400`.

The photos are read as the caller lists that resource, in one query for the whole page: its tenant, row filter, soft delete and readable fields apply, each file comes as that resource's list returns it, with its placeholder when the caller may read that field, and the [scan guard](#safety) checks the lookup like a list. A caller who cannot list the resource, or read and use the relation, the file field or the sorted fields, gets `photos: {}`, as they would for a resource or field that does not exist, so `photos` never tells it exists; so does a list of a resource with a composite key.

### Maps

`:map` answers a map of a resource's records at their position, two filterable number fields in decimal degrees (`latitude` and `longitude` name them) and MapLibre's `zoom`, a whole number from 0 to 22. The map's bounding box is part of the AIP-160 `filter`, with the list's own filter: `(rooms >= 3) AND lat >= 51.9 AND lat <= 52.1 AND lng >= 4.2 AND lng <= 4.5`, or `(lng >= 170 OR lng <= -170)` across the antimeridian. When up to 200 records match, or from zoom 16 on, `items` holds them (at most 200, in `order_by` order) as a list returns them, and `buckets` is empty. Otherwise `buckets` counts them per cell of a grid about 64 pixels across at the zoom, square on a Web Mercator map and fixed as it pans, the fullest 1,000 cells, each as `{ count, latitude, longitude, bounds: { south, west, north, east } }`: the records' mean position and the bounds around them, which a map zooms to when the bucket is chosen. `items` is then empty, and records without a position are in no bucket. `total_size` counts the matches either way, up to 10,000 when `items` holds them, as `count=exact` does, the planner's estimate above that. Postgres counts and groups the records, so an index on the position serves the bounding box.

## Access

Access is resolved once per request and resource ([`resolveAccess`](https://docs.protobase.net/api/schema/functions/resolveaccess/), see [Login with Better Auth](auth.md) for roles and capabilities), and everything downstream uses the result:

- **Operations**: a denied operation is `403`; a resource the caller can do nothing with does not exist for them (`404` everywhere, absent from `/meta` and the OpenAPI document).
- **Readable fields**: the caller works with a restricted model that has only the fields they may read. `filter`, `order_by`, `fields`, `search(...)`, `:facets`, `:aggregate`, `:histogram`, `:series`, `:map`, `:seek` and `:search` bodies are checked against it, so a hidden field is refused exactly like an unknown one (same status, same message and hint, nothing that says it exists). List, get, create, update and delete responses contain readable fields only, and queries select only those columns.
- **Sensitive fields** are readable fields that no response carries and no request may name, except `:reveal`; they can be written. See [Sensitive fields and audit](#sensitive-fields-and-audit).
- **Writable fields**: only fields the caller may write and read are accepted, and [write-only](access.md#write-only-fields) ones; any other is `400`, worded as unknown (hidden) or read-only.
- **Row filters**: a rule that returns a filter (`.own`, `.team`) narrows every read (list, get, aggregates) and the rows a write may target; the database applies it, so it may use columns the caller cannot see. A row outside it is a `404`.
- **Record-level rules** (a rule that needs the record, such as `status != 'locked'`) run in the write transaction with the stored record; a filter they return is checked in the database against the row as written, and a miss rolls the write back with `403`.
- **`.own` on create**: when the create rule is limited to rows, the owner field is set to the caller unless given, and a row owned by someone else is refused with `403`.
- **Seeking**: `:seek` resolves a row position to a page on the server, inside the caller's tenant, row filter and filter. No anchor value, column statistic or boundary token is ever returned (table-wide statistics include rows the caller may not see), only the page and the tokens of its own rows.
- **ETags**: with a read-only `version` or `updated_at` column the ETag is a hash of that column's exact text, so it never shows a hidden value yet moves on every change. Without one it is a hash of the fields the caller may read, sensitive ones excluded: a change to a field they cannot read, or to a sensitive field, does not change their ETag.
- **Errors** never contain values of fields the caller cannot read; database errors leave out constraint and column names.

`options.roles` (from `defineRoles`) makes an operation without an explicit rule need the matching capability (`orders.update`), and limits each role to the [fields and rows](access.md#capabilities) its capabilities list; `options.defaultAccess: 'allow' | 'deny'` overrides the capability check. Without either, operations without a rule are allowed (single-admin projects).

### Record permissions

Get responses carry `permissions: { update, delete, fields }`, where `fields` maps each readable field to `edit` or `read` for this record (hidden fields are not listed). List items carry `permissions: { update, delete }` too, decided in the database in one extra query per page; turn it off for a resource with `options.rowPermissions: { except: ['resource'] }` (or `false` for all). They only inform the UI: every write is checked again. A resource cannot have a field named `permissions` or `etag`.

### `/meta` and OpenAPI per caller

`/meta` returns, per caller: the resources they can do anything with as restricted models (hidden fields absent, `readOnly` unless writable, [write-only](access.md#write-only-fields) fields marked `writeOnly`), the view for their roles ([`pickView`](https://docs.protobase.net/api/schema/functions/pickview/)) with every reference to a hidden field removed (columns, sort, search, filters, layout, chart, title, search result) and the [related sections](ui-config.md#related-records) they cannot use, `permissions[resource]` as `{ read, create, update, delete, conditional }`, the [user menu](user-menu.md) as `userMenu` and the [bottom bar](bottom-bar.md) of their active role as `bottomBar`, each without the resources and pages they cannot see, and the [composed pages](layouts.md#access) as `pages`, each without the elements that name what they cannot see or do, and, for a caller with the `admin` or `ai` role, the [assistant](assistant.md#who-sees-it) backend as `assistant: { url }` when the app has one, and, for a caller with the `admin` role, the [runtime updates](versioning.md#runtime-updates) endpoint as `runtime: { url }` when the app has one, and, for everyone, the style of the record page's [maps](ui-config.md#maps) as `maps: { style }` when the app has one, the [language](languages.md) of its screens as `locale` when it sets one, and the Protobase version the server runs as `protobaseVersion`. When that version changes under an open page, the admin app keeps what the page shows, stops reading `/meta`, and offers to reload the page, asking first while a form holds unsaved changes or a save is under way. `conditional` lists the operations allowed only for some records (a row filter or a record-level rule decides). A view's sidebar group ([`nav.recent`](sidebar.md#recent-records)) is dropped when it uses a field they cannot read. The ETag hashes all of it, so it differs per user and per roles. The OpenAPI document is generated the same way: record and body schemas have only the readable and writable fields, and methods the caller may not use are left out. Its `servers` are relative to the document (`v1` for the resources, `.` for the system endpoints), and `/api/docs` loads `openapi.json` beside it, so both are right on any host and under any prefix the API is reached at.

## Sensitive fields and audit

A field declared [`.sensitive()`](data-config.md#sensitive-fields) is in `/meta` (marked `sensitive: true`), in record `permissions.fields` and in create and update bodies, but in no list, get, `:search`, `:seek`, write or batch response, and `filter`, `order_by`, `fields` and the aggregates refuse it like an unknown field. `POST /{resource}/{key}:reveal` with `{ "field": "<name>" }` returns one record's value. It needs read access to the record and the field: another tenant's record, a row outside the caller's row filter or a key that does not exist is a `404`, a field the caller cannot read or that is not sensitive a `400`. An [encrypted field](data-config.md#encrypted-fields)'s reveal decrypts its value, and an empty one reveals `null`; a value that does not decrypt is a `500` reported to the operator, without an audit event. An update that changes the key of a record with encrypted fields is a `400` `key-change-unsupported`.

Before answering, the server publishes an audit event to `options.audit`, and when publishing fails the reveal fails (`500`), so no value leaves without its event. The event never holds the value:

```ts
type AuditEvent = {
  type: 'field.revealed'
  at: string                                  // ISO 8601
  actor: { id: string | number; roles: string[] }
  tenant?: string | number                    // the caller's organization, for tenant-scoped resources
  resource: string
  recordKey: string                           // as in the record's URL
  field: string
  origin: { userAgent?: string; forwardedFor?: string } // from the request headers
}
```

With [organizations](auth.md#organizations), someone with a global role switching into an organization they are not a member of publishes `{ type: 'organization.entered', at, actor, organization, origin }` first, where `actor.roles` are their global roles; a failed publish refuses the switch. `AuditEvent` is the union of the two.

### Audit events

`options.audit` is an `AuditQueue`, `{ publish(event): Promise<void> }`, set in `protobase.config.ts` (`options: { roles, audit }`). The default, `consoleAuditQueue()`, prints each event to the console as one `[audit] {...}` JSON line and keeps nothing; a queue that stores or forwards events replaces it there.

## Filters

`filter` and `order_by` are AIP-160 and AIP-132 text, checked against the model (filterable and sortable fields only). Functions: `in(field, v, ...)`, `search("text")` and bare words (every word, ignoring case, anywhere inside one of the resource's search fields, so `port` finds "Portfolio"; `%`, `_` and `\` are literal; a [`digitsEnd`](data-config.md#resource) field matches only the end of its digits), `similar(field, "text")`, `regex(field, "pattern")`, `isNull(field)`, `now()` with offsets such as `now() - 7d`. A filter is capped at 10,000 characters in a query string and 200,000 in a `:search` body.

## Writes

Create, update and delete share one pipeline (`write-pipeline.ts`):

1. the caller is authenticated and, for tenant-scoped resources, has a tenant (`403` otherwise);
2. unknown fields, read-only fields and the tenant column in the body are refused, each value is validated by its field's zod schema (an empty string for a text field without `.optional()` counts as missing: `required`, or its default on a create), then the resource's `.validate()` rules run (`400` with `errors: [{ field, code, message }]`); what needs the network is checked before the transaction opens, such as the address of a [webhook subscription](webhooks.md)'s URL;
3. one transaction with `SET LOCAL statement_timeout`; the row is locked with `FOR UPDATE`; another tenant's key, or a soft-deleted row, is a `404`;
4. the access rule runs, then `If-Match` is compared with the ETag (`428` when missing on PATCH, `412` when stale);
5. the write, then `writeHooks` inside the same transaction (a hook that throws rolls the write back). Audit logging and the admin store plug in here;
6. once it commits, the files it took out of its rows are scheduled for deletion (see [Deleting files](files.md#deleting-files)), so the transaction never waits on the storage.

**ETag**: the `version` or `updated_at` column when the resource has a read-only one (bumped on every update, so no trigger is needed; the ETag keeps the column's full microsecond text), otherwise a hash of the exposed fields. It is computed from the row itself, so lists need no extra query.

**`etag` property**: every record in a get, list, `:search`, create or update response carries its current version as `etag` (the value of the `ETag` header, [AIP-154](https://google.aip.dev/154)), so a grid row can be updated or deleted without a get. It survives `fields` selection. A resource cannot have a field named `etag` (startup error); a body containing `etag` is a `400` that points at `If-Match`.

**If-Match** is required on PATCH (`428` without it). On DELETE it is optional: without it the current version is deleted. When sent it must match, otherwise `412`; `*` matches whatever the current version is (RFC 9110).

**Prefer**: create and update return the record by default; `Prefer: return=minimal` returns no body (`201`/`204`). Delete returns `204`, or the record with `Prefer: return=representation`.

The rules behind these steps are described under [Access](#access).

## Batch writes

`POST /api/v1:batchWrite` takes `{ ops: [...] }` (`{ operations: [...] }` is accepted too), at most 500, run in order inside ONE transaction, so check constraints and triggers see one consistent state. Each operation goes through the same write pipeline as a single write (validation, access with row filters and record-level rules, tenant, ETags, hooks), access is checked per operation, and the operations may span resources.

| `op` | fields |
| --- | --- |
| `create` | `resource`, `data`, `ref?` |
| `update` | `resource`, `key`, `etag` (required, `*` allowed), `data` |
| `delete` | `resource`, `key`, `etag?` |
| `reorder` | `resource`, `field`, `keys` (in final order), `start` (optional, 1 by default), `etags` (per key text) |

- **Keys** are the URL text (`a,b` when composite), a number, a list of parts, or a reference.
- **`$ref`**: `ref: 'invoice'` on a create names the record; later operations use `{ "$ref": "invoice" }` as a key, a key part, or a value in `data` (it stands for that record's key, or with `{ "$ref": "invoice", "field": "number" }` a readable field's value). A ref must come after its create.
- **`reorder`** sets `field` to `start`, `start` + 1, ... in the order of `keys`, so a long list sends only the stretch that moved, and writes only the records whose value changes, each as an ordinary update (so each needs its `etags` entry, and hooks see each). To work with a non-deferrable unique index such as `(invoice_id, position)`, the changing records are first moved out of the range in use, in the same transaction and without touching their ETags: above the highest value of the column, or, when a check constraint refuses that (checked with a savepoint), below the lowest one. Then they get their final values, which collide with nothing. The field must be an integer the caller may write; the keys must all exist and be visible to the caller. When it is the resource's [position with `after`](ui-config.md#ranked-after-what-they-depend-on), a reorder that puts a record at or above a record it depends on, or one of those at or below it, fails with `409` and the type `ranks-above-dependency`, naming both keys in `record` and `dependsOn`; pairs out of order before it do not count.
- **Result**: `{ results: [...] }`, one entry per operation in order: `create` and `update` give `record` and `etag`, `delete` gives `deleted: true`, `reorder` gives `records` (every key in order, with its etag).
- **Failure**: nothing is written. The problem is the failing operation's own (`400`, `403`, `404`, `409`, `412`, `428`, ...) with `operation` (its index), `op` and `resource` added. A stale ETag anywhere is a `412` for the whole batch.

## Authentication

Real login is [Better Auth](auth.md). Lower level:

`authenticate(request)` returns `{ user: { id, roles }, tenant? }` or throws `unauthorized(...)` (a `401` problem), or `new MissingCredentials(...)` (also a `401`) when the request carries no credential at all. Shipped: `jwtAuthenticator({ jwksUrl | keys, issuer?, audience?, rolesClaim?, tenantClaim?, tenant? })`, which verifies a bearer token with `jose` (`sub` is the user id; `tenant` fixes the tenant instead of reading a claim), and `betterAuthAuthenticator` on top of it ([Login with Better Auth](auth.md)). No code path treats a request as a user without verifying a credential; the one exception is the [anonymous role](access.md#anonymous-access), which the resources API gives a request that has none, when the project defines it.

## CORS

The API sends no CORS headers until it has something to allow: other websites in `options.cors` (a list of origins, or `'*'` for any), which defaults to `PROTOBASE_CORS_ORIGINS` (`*` or comma separated http and https origins), other [origins of the app](auth.md#several-origins), which are always allowed, or a [mobile section](../guides/mobile-app.md), which allows the app's Capacitor origins, `capacitor://localhost` and `https://localhost`. `PROTOBASE_CORS_ORIGINS` refuses other schemes at startup.

- It covers `/api/*` but Better Auth's `/api/auth/*`, which checks origins itself (the mobile app [signs in](../guides/mobile-app.md) through native HTTP, outside CORS), and [API functions](../guides/api-functions.md) with a `cors` of their own; supabase-js's [`/api/sb`](auth.md#supabase-js-and-supabasessr) is under it too.
- An allowed origin gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` with its name and `Vary: Origin`, or `*` with `'*'`. No credentials: browser code calls the API with a bearer token.
- Preflights are answered before authentication, for `authorization`, `content-type`, `if-match`, `if-none-match` and supabase-js's `apikey`, `x-client-info` and `x-supabase-api-version`, and kept for 10 minutes. `Location`, `ETag`, `X-Meta-Version` and `X-Protobase-Warning` are exposed.
- An API whose resources another app draws as [remote resources](remote-resources.md#cors) lists that app's origin here.

## Safety

- Every request runs in a transaction with `SET LOCAL statement_timeout` (`statementTimeoutMs`, default 15 s); a timeout is `504`. List, search, get, histogram, series, map and seek transactions are read-only.
- **Scan guard**: a list, `:search`, `:seek`, `:map` page, card photos, `:facets` and `:aggregate` read only columns an index serves, so they stay cheap however many rows match. The server reads each table's valid indexes from the catalog once, then checks every column the caller's filter, the role's row filter, the sort's first field and a facet's or an aggregate's grouped field read:
  - Comparisons, `in`, null checks, sorts and facets need a btree index with the column as a key, every key before it pinned by the query: by `=` or `in` in the filter (outside `OR` and `NOT`), by the tenant or by soft delete. `(for_sale, status, published_at desc)` serves `for_sale = true AND status = "available"` sorted by `published_at desc`, but not `status` alone. `=` on text may use a pg_trgm index instead.
  - Patterns (`name = "*port*"`), `regex()`, `similar()` and `search()` need a pg_trgm (GIN or GiST) index on each column they read, a `digitsEnd` search field one on its digits; JSON `field:value` needs a GIN index.
  - A partial index counts for nothing, and a resource on a plain view or a foreign table, which has no indexes of its own, is not checked.

  A column without one is a `400` `expensive-query` problem that names it, with `columns` (each `{ field, column, use, need, suggestion }`) and a `create index` `suggestion`; `scanGuard: { mode: 'warn' }` answers with an `X-Protobase-Warning` header instead, `'off'` disables it. The indexes are read when a table is first queried and kept for the process lifetime, so restart the server after adding one. [`protobase doctor`](cli.md#doctor) judges every read the config makes by the same rule against the database's indexes, so a missing index fails it before a deploy instead of a page after.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with `type` (`urn:protobase:problem:<slug>`), `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`. Filter and `order_by` errors add `parameter` and `errors: [{ code, message, hint, span: { start, end } }]`; invalid parameters add `errors: [{ parameter, message }]`. A create or update whose body fails the checks is `invalid-record` with `errors: [{ field, code, message, params }]`, `code` one of `required`, `invalid-value`, `read-only`, `unknown-field` and `invalid-record` (a `.validate()` rule); `params` is the limit an invalid value broke, such as `{ min }`, `{ max }` or a decimal's `{ precision, scale }`. Database constraint failures map to `409` or `400` without the raw message. A create or update that writes the position of a resource with `after` so a record ranks at or above one it depends on is a `409` `ranks-above-dependency`, as in a [`reorder`](#batch-writes). A delete that other records still point at is a `409` `conflict` with `blockedBy: { resource, field? }`: their resource, when the caller may list it, and its relation field pointing at the record, when they may filter by it, so a client can open those records; the admin app's toast names them, such as "Orders still point at this company.", with a link to that list. Postgres names one table of them only, so `blockedBy` holds one resource; anything unexpected is a `500` with a fixed detail, reported to `options.onUnhandledError` and, when it is set, the [error tracker](#error-reporting).

| Status | Slugs |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | `invalid-filter`, `invalid-order-by`, `invalid-parameter`, `invalid-key`, `invalid-record`, `malformed-json`, `expensive-query`, query-layer codes |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` |
| 403 | `access-denied`, `tenant-required` |
| 404 | `not-found` |
| 409 | `conflict` |
| 412 / 428 | `precondition-failed` / `precondition-required` |
| 503 | `read-only`: the database refuses writes, as during a deploy's write freeze; send the write again after `Retry-After` |
| 504 | `statement-timeout` |

### Error reporting

An app can send its errors to an error tracker of its own: [Sentry](https://sentry.io) or one that speaks its protocol, such as [Bugsink](https://www.bugsink.com) or [GlitchTip](https://glitchtip.com). It is off until a DSN, the address the tracker gives a project, is set in `options.errorReporting` or `PROTOBASE_SENTRY_DSN`; without one nothing is loaded or sent.

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  options: { errorReporting: { dsn: 'https://<key>@errors.example.com/42', environment: 'staging' } },
})
```

- **Server:** every `500` with the request it failed, under `dev`, `serve` and the runtime, besides `options.onUnhandledError` or the console. Under `serve`, the runtime and `worker`, an uncaught exception or unhandled rejection too, which then still ends the process with exit code 1.
- **Admin app:** uncaught errors and the errors of components that fail to draw. `/api/meta` names the DSN to every signed-in caller, as a browser app always shows its own.
- Errors only, with no performance tracing. Before an event leaves, the values of authorization headers, cookies, passwords, tokens and other credentials, in fields and in URLs, are replaced by `[Filtered]`.
- `environment` names the deployment in the tracker; without it the tracker's default, `production`. `errorReporting: false` turns reporting off whatever the environment says. A DSN that is no `http(s)` URL with a key and a project id stops startup.
